entry: New: Expeditions, in the new Fleet Lab (toolbar, Desktop: Menu, Empire). Send one idle, hand-flown ship away from the routes for 12 ticks; it cannot trade meanwhile (that is the cost) and comes back with credits, research points, a curio for your 12-piece cabinet, or just the view. The odds are written next to the button and in its tooltip, and nothing is ever unlucky twice running: after two empty trips the next always finds something, and every fifth trip without a curio always finds one. Two new achievements.

New: Market Weather, an optional switch in the Market panel. Now and then one good has a boom (+30%) or a slump (-25%) for 20 to 40 ticks, and the good that depends on it follows at half strength. A one-line headline on the map names the event, and the Almanac explains the leading indicators: dock gossip names the colony 12 ticks ahead and says boom or slump 5 ticks ahead, so you can stockpile in time. Nothing is permanent, and see five events through for the Storm Watcher achievement.

New: Blackout, an optional harder way to play (Market panel). With it on, the map goes dark, the sparklines are hidden and prices show only as ranges until you buy the information back: a price feed (250 credits, or research Market Insight) and a star chart (200 credits, or research Galaxy Expansion). The economy itself does not change. Switch it on before your first sale and keep it on to the endgame to earn the Dark Run achievement, a stamp in the Charter ledger and a mark beside the title.

New: a practice sandbox. Press Practice sandbox (Desktop: Menu, Empire) to try a separate practice corporation with a large balance that never runs out, every research node known (so every system and route is open), every ship bought and no route hazards. A banner says Sandbox: nothing here is saved, nothing in it earns an achievement or lets you renew the charter, and Leave sandbox puts your real corporation back exactly as it was. Saving while you are in it saves your real corporation. Also fixed: a colony's neglect counter above 40 is no longer reset to 0 when a save is loaded.

New: a Copy result button in the Summary copies a one-line result (total profit, colonies developed, ships, endgame) to share. Earned achievements now have a Share button, and a Credits link sits at the bottom of the page (in the Help menu on Desktop).

New: a Pause, 1x, 2x and 4x control sits under the toolbar (Space pauses or resumes, [ and ] change the speed). Faster only means the game ticks more often, never that anything is skipped, and nothing at all happens while it is paused. New: a setting, on by default, pauses the game while this browser tab is hidden and tells you when you come back; switch it off in Settings if you want it to keep running in the background.

Captains, moods and records: a ship that becomes a veteran hauler earns a captain's seat, and from the new Captains panel you pick who sits in it (Frugal, Lucky Trader, Night Owl or Perfectionist, each with a perk and a trade-off, and each can be moved to another ship once per charter). Colonies now have moods that follow how you treat them: Grateful (a small premium on sales), Demanding (a bigger answer to a concession) and Opportunistic (a discount on Invest while its need is low), shown as a circle, triangle or square on the map and explained in the colony panel. Stockpile trades leave a dashed ghost line on the price sparkline showing where the price was before. The Ledger shows throughput (units per ship per 100 ticks) and a ribbon of your earned achievement badges, the title carries a charter crest (shape plus word), and the Charter panel keeps a career log of every finished charter. A new Effects switch in Settings turns off the sparks, dock rings and ribbon glow. Two new achievements.

Trade Empire now has a Desktop layout for wide windows with a mouse: the colony network map fills the window, your ships sit in a column beside it (load, depart and automate without scrolling the page), Fleet Priority and the Trade Guild sit in a strip above the map, and the needs-at-a-glance chips and the last sale sit under it. Total profit, automation slots and research points are chips along the top. Colonies, the Market (with stockpiles and trade posts), Research, About, the Charter, the Summary, achievements and settings open as windows over the map from the icons or the Menu (Esc), and Desktop has its own tutorial. The Classic layout is unchanged and your save works in both; switch from the opening screen or the Menu.

Renew the Charter: at the endgame, founding a new corporation is now renewing the charter. Each renewal earns charter points, spent in the new Charter panel on a small permanent perk tree (Routes, Automation, Colonies and Reputation, twelve modest perks that carry into every later charter; nothing stacks freely). Every renewal after the first opens with new founding conditions: two home colonies start thriving and connected, and the rest start stretched. The panel also holds a lifetime ledger (goods moved, routes established, charters completed across every charter), and after your first endgame you can opt into a harder charter with faster market saturation and quicker-fading colony needs for one extra charter point. Three new achievements. Saves that already renewed are migrated (each past renewal counts as a completed charter with its points), and nothing changes for anyone who never renews.

Light theme polish: the market and colony meter fills, sparklines, research points, crashed-price text, profit and endgame readouts, idle-ship warning and captions were darkened for readable contrast on the light theme, the mobile needs-strip chips no longer keep pale text, and the star map keeps a dark backing. Dark mode is unchanged (Y11b).

Story mode: an optional Story panel follows your trading company from one ship and one contract through the home system, the Kepler Cluster, the Rift Colonies and the Umbral Deep to the fully-automated endgame and a new corporation. There is one short chapter for each achievement, plus one for reaching the Rift Colonies and one for the Umbral Deep. Chapters appear only as you earn them, a loaded save brings its chapters back, and the Story on/off pill hides the panel. It never changes a save or how the game plays (W1).

New fourth cluster, the Umbral Deep: three colonies (Nadir Foundry, Hush Cryostat, Tenebra Loom) making Neutronium, Superfluid and Aerogel, the priciest goods yet. It takes the deepest research in the game: Deep Survey (240, needs Outer Reaches) and then Umbral Reach (360). Its colonies pay the most and are the hardest to keep fed, its developed colonies need Rift goods, it can host a trade post, and the map grew taller to fit it. Saves that haven't reached it are unchanged, and loading one now also sends any ship parked at a still-locked colony back home.

New Trade Guild: now and then it offers a bulk contract (deliver a number of units of a good to a colony before a deadline) for a bonus on top of the normal sale. Optional, and missing one costs nothing. Two new achievements, Guild Partner and Guild Favorite.

New Legacy: once you reach the endgame you can found a new corporation. Everything resets to a fresh start, but you keep your achievements and gain a permanent legacy bonus (extra starting credits and a small boost to every sale, up to five levels).
Achievement cards now show "Earned by N% of players" once enough real save data exists for that achievement (site-wide goal, Z1/Z27b).
Added a keyboard-shortcuts help overlay: press ? to see it, Esc to close it or whichever panel is open (site-wide goal, Z4).
Settings panel: added a "Reset to Default" button that resets text size and reduce-motion back to their defaults in one click (site-wide goal, folded from A26).

Colony loyalty: a colony left badly under-supplied for a long stretch now asks for a one-time concession (80 credits to restore 30% satisfaction). Ignoring it costs nothing; it just lapses and only returns after a cooldown.
The map now shows a brief pulse when a ship leaves a colony (a ring growing outward) or arrives at one (a ring closing in). Nothing is drawn if you have reduced motion on.
Trade posts: once every automation slot is in use you can establish a trade post in each reachable star system (400 credits each), earning 2 credits per tick with no ship needed.

Market speculation: every good now has a small stockpile (15 units). Buy 5 while a price is crashed, hold it, and sell once the price recovers. Buying pushes the price up, selling pushes it down and pays a 10% fee.
Colony investment: each undeveloped colony has an Invest button that spends 60 credits to add 10 units of development progress, so spare credits can speed up a colony's growth and specialization.

Research specialization: after Automation Expansion II you choose an Automation path (+10% on automated ships' sales, then +1 automation slot) or a Market path (prices recover 50% faster, then drop 30% less per sale). Picking one closes the other for good.
When you buy ship 5 or 6 you now choose its type: Balanced, Cargo-heavy (carries 50% more but is one tick slower) or Fast (one tick quicker but carries 25% less).

New optional Route hazards and Route insurance toggles in the Market prices panel: with hazards on, 8% of loaded arrivals lose their cargo; insurance costs 1 credit per ship in transit per tick and refunds 75% of a lost trip.
Diplomatic relations: units you deliver between star systems now build relations (3 levels), each giving a permanent +5% on every sale.
New optional Seasonal demand toggle in the Market prices panel: every 30 ticks two goods are in demand and sell for 25% more, with the current and next pair always shown. Nothing is ever marked down.
New Trade almanac in the Market prices panel: each good's baseline price, typical range, and which colony makes and needs it.
Hover over the endgame galaxy dots to see which background world you're pointing at.
A small spark/particle burst now plays briefly on a high-value sale (200+ credits).

Round-2 quality pass: ship name reset, veteran-hauler badge, route trend arrows, fleet-efficiency and galaxy overview in Summary, map legend and Fleet Priority ring tooltip, crash recovery ETA, locked-research tooltips, labeled price-now marker, needs-met average.
Confirm-before-spending dialogs added for automating a ship or unlocking research (both rare, irreversible, high-cost actions).

All 14 milestones shipped: manual trade loop, colony needs and market economics, automation, the 2D map, research tree, colony specialization, fleet-level automation, galaxy expansion, and the fully-automated endgame. Followed by a bug-fix pass: Kepler Cluster map labels no longer collide; hub-link paths corrected; then space-theme visual pass: starfield background, glass panels, gradient buttons; then skippable tutorial, a How to Play page, and a mobile sticky HUD. Also: a condensed colony-needs strip now docks to the bottom of the screen on mobile so it's visible alongside the ship panels. Also: achievements added: 19 achievements, in-game panel, unlock toast, hub dashboard link. Gap-closing pass: colorblind-safety audit confirmed (automated vs. manual ships already distinguished by shape, not just color). Also (2026-09-19): Settings panel: adjustable text size and a Reduce Motion toggle.
